chunks: And everything in this book that is narrated from Abu Wallad Al-Hannat has been transmitted by me from my father - may Allah be pleased with him - from Sa'd ibn Abdullah, from Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq Al-Nahdi, from Al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from Abu Wallad Al-Hannat, whose name was Hafs ibn Salim, a freed servant of Banu Makhzum.

key_terms.أَبِي وَلَّادَ الْحَنَّاطِ: Abu Wallad Al-Hannat, a narrator known for his transmissions in Shia hadith literature.
key_terms.بَنِي مَخْزُومٍ: Banu Makhzum, a prominent clan of the Quraysh tribe.
key_terms.رَضِيَ اللَّهُ عَنْهُ: May Allah be pleased with him, a phrase of respect often used for the narrator's father.
key_terms.مَوْلَى: Mawla, a freed servant or client, indicating a social relationship of patronage.

ai.seo_question: Who is Abu Wallad Al-Hannat and what is his full name in Shia hadith sources?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Saduq provides a precise biographical verification of Abu Wallad Al-Hannat (Hafs ibn Salim), identifying him as a mawla of the Banu Makhzum to establish his credibility within the Shia scholarly tradition. By explicitly tracing the chain through his father and other key narrators like Al-Haytham ibn Abi Masruq, the text underscores the rigorous attention to detail in hadith authentication (ilm al-rijal) characteristic of the Kufan school.
